responses.text: Taiwan’s legislature passed amendments to the Tobacco Hazards Prevention Act on January 12, 2023.
The amended Act took effect on March 22, 2023.
It prohibits the manufacture, import, sale, supply, display, advertising and use of electronic cigarettes and similar products.
Designated products such as heated tobacco must pass a health-risk assessment before they may be manufactured, imported or sold.
Components necessary to use designated products must be submitted for review with the products.
Approved designated products cannot be sold through vending machines or e-commerce methods that cannot verify age.
The law bars specified promotions and advertising, free commercial supply, and supply to people under 20.
Taiwan raised the legal smoking age from 18 to 20.
Tobacco-package pictorial warnings increased from 35% to 50% of the container area.
The Act bars additives prohibited by the central authority, whose announced draft list covered floral, fruit, chocolate and mint flavors.
The expanded smoke-free locations include universities, kindergartens, infant-care centers and home childcare premises.
Bars and nightclubs permit smoking only in independently separated smoking rooms.
Manufacturing or importing electronic cigarettes can incur a maximum NT$50 million penalty, while use can be fined NT$2,000–10,000.
The Health Ministry said the previous legal basis inadequately addressed emerging electronic and heated products and flavored products that entice use, with the greatest harm falling on adolescents.
The ministry said it drew on the WHO Framework Convention on Tobacco Control, international experience and stakeholder views.
The United Arab Emirates made e-cigarette use subject to its federal tobacco-control law and prohibited vaping inside offices and other enclosed spaces.
That law prohibits tobacco sales to people under 18.
It also forbids smoking in a private car carrying a child under 12 and in houses of worship, educational, health and sports facilities.
The UAE additionally prohibits tobacco advertising and automatic tobacco-vending or distribution devices.
The health ministry worked with the telecommunications regulator to block websites promoting electronic nicotine-delivery systems.
The ministry emphasized tobacco-product dangers, while UAE doctors had argued that e-cigarettes could create a new generation of smokers.
As non-youth context, reported adult tobacco-smoking prevalence declined from 11.1% in 2010 to 9.1% in 2018.
Russia’s State Duma has considered bill No. 332229-8, initiated by 398 deputies.
The bill would prohibit sales to minors of both nicotine-containing and nicotine-free vapes.
Vapes would be sold only in retail stores and could not be openly displayed.
The proposal would also exclude flavored nicotine products from circulation.
Additional proposed restrictions cover sales of devices and parts at fairs, exhibitions, remotely, through machines or by delivery, as well as discounts.
Its explanatory reasoning cites police monitoring of serious incidents and regional nicotine-liquid poisonings, including fatalities.
A separate proposed Russian retail ban cited a tenfold rise in adolescent vaping between 2011 and early 2023.
Hong Kong legislators passed a law on October 21, 2021 banning the sale, import, manufacture, distribution and advertising of e-cigarettes and heated-tobacco devices.
Hong Kong’s government justified the law by saying these products contain harmful substances and scheduled commencement six months after passage.
Ukraine’s parliament approved anti-tobacco bill No. 4358 at second reading on December 16, 2021, after which parliamentary and presidential signatures were still required.
The Ukrainian measure equated vapes and heated-tobacco devices with cigarettes for indoor and public-place use, advertising and youth-sale restrictions.
It also prohibited flavored cigarettes, promotional sales and tastings, and advertising on transport, at concerts and on social media.
Colombia’s Law 2354 of 2024 subjects vaping products to existing tobacco controls, prohibits their use by minors and applies restrictions in enclosed or public places such as restaurants.
Colombia also requires package risk warnings and government health-risk education campaigns directed especially to users, children and young people.

The collection reports no measured post-law change in youth-vaping rates for Taiwan, the UAE, Russia, Hong Kong, Ukraine or Colombia, and gives neither the UAE confirmation date nor the proposal date for Russian bill No. 332229-8.

The state Duma intends to tighten the regulation of sales of vape and electronic cigarettes
NEWS
Akhmed Sadulaev
News Editor
Akhmed Sadulaev
State Duma deputies are preparing a bill to tighten the rules for the turnover of electronic cigarettes, vape and liquids for them in Russia.
If the law is passed, it will be possible to sell the devices only in retail stores.
The state Duma intends to tighten the regulation of sales of vape and electronic cigarettes
The document includes a ban on:
• Sale of “devices for the consumption of nicotine products ” and their components at fairs, exhibitions, remotely, through vending machines, as well as their delivery.
• Issue and circulation of electronic cigarettes with flavors and additives “in order to reduce the attractiveness of these products for minors ”.
• Open display and demonstration of devices in stores.
In this case, the sale will be carried out on a list with names.
• Discounts on devices.
In addition, legislators intend to limit advertising with images, descriptions or episodic mentions of devices, and also prohibit its display to children under 12 years of age.
The purpose of the document, according to the text, is “to protect the life and health of minors. ”
Among the authors of the project: the speaker of the chamber Vyacheslav Volodin, leaders of factions, vice-speakers Irina Yarovaya, Peter Tolstoy and others.
“Almost 400 deputies from all factions signed the bill, ” Tolstoy wrote in his Telegram.
According to the politician, “other steps will follow, ” including tougher liability for violating the law.

The third reading of the Legislative Yuan amended some provisions of the Tobacco Harm Prevention Act to regulate heating of cigarettes and vehicles, prohibit electronic cigarettes, and raise the smoking ban age to 20 years old. (Photo / pixabay)
(Taiwan English News / Zhu Mingzhu Taipei Report) The Legislative Yuan today (12) amended some provisions of the Tobacco Harm Prevention Act, including the control of heated cigarettes and vehicles, the prohibition of electronic cigarettes, the increase of the smoking ban age to 20 years, and the expansion of smoking ban places.
The new law stipulates that manufacturers must submit a health risk assessment before manufacturing or importing hot cigarettes, and prohibit specific promotional or advertising activities after listing.
According to the National Health Administration, e-cigarettes, hot cigarettes and the addition of various flavors of enticing products have appeared in the world.
As the current regulatory law is not comprehensive enough, it is increasingly harmful to people's health, especially teenagers.
Referring to the World Health Organization Framework Convention on Tobacco Control (WHO FCTC), international experience and opinions from various sectors, the Ministry of Health and Welfare studied and drafted amendments to the Tobacco Hazard Prevention Law, which were submitted by the Executive Yuan to the Legislative Yuan for deliberation on January 13, 111.
The third reading through the article of civilization, the future will be accepted to heat cigarettes, prohibit electronic cigarettes.
Designated tobacco products announced by the central competent authority, whether or not they are new types of products or have already been listed, as long as the health risk is unknown or a specific health risk is newly discovered, they shall apply for a health risk assessment review, and after the review and approval, they shall not be allowed to start or continue to manufacture, import, or sell.
If approved, it is prohibited to sell certain promotional and advertising activities, or to sell in a manner that does not recognize the age of the consumer, such as vending, electronic shopping, etc.).
In addition, the business premises shall not be provided free of charge, and no one shall be allowed to supply them to anyone under the age of 20.
At the same time, the smoking ban will be extended to colleges and universities, kindergartens, childcare centers and home-style nurseries.

In Russia, proposed to completely ban the sale of vape
21
Ayman Amanzholova
[email protected]
The authors of the bill cite data according to which the number of teenagers using vapes at the beginning of last year increased 10 times compared to 2011, Kazpravda.kz reports with reference to TASS
Photo: Kazpravda.kz / Adilbek Tauekelov
Deputies from the LDPR, CPRF, “Fair Russia – For the Truth ” and“ New People ” factions have developed a bill to completely ban the retail sale of nicotine and nicotine-free vape in Russia.
“It is prohibited to retail sale of nicotine (including synthesized) or its derivatives, including nicotine salts, as well as nicotine-containing and nicotine-free liquids and devices for their delivery, ” the text of the bill says.
As told TASS one of the developers of the initiative, the head of the State Duma Committee on labor, social policy and veterans Affairs Yaroslav Nilov (LDPR), currently continues the process of collecting signatures under the initiative, as well as consultations on the document.
According to him, soon the bill will be submitted to the state Duma.
The authors of the document cite data according to which the number of adolescents using vape at the beginning of 2023 increased by 10 times compared to 2011.
According to the explanatory note, vaping is promoted as a safe alternative to conventional cigarettes, “but it causes irreparable harm to the health of both the smoker and the people around him. ”
"Doctors even distinguish a special disease - vape associated lung damage, reminiscent of the symptoms and manifestations of pneumonia.
E-cigarette smokers, as well as ordinary smokers, also form a nicotine addiction, ” the authors of the bill note.
According to them, this ban will cause a loss of federal budget revenues.
However, preserving the health of the nation, especially young people, is much more important for the future of our country.
As for the possibility of increasing the illegal turnover of vapes, it is still quite large, its suppression is the task of law enforcement agencies, ” the authors explain.

UAE Bans Vaping in Public Spaces

    Vaping e-cigarettes is prohibited inside offices and closed spaces across the United Arab Emirates (UAE), the health ministry has confirmed. The use of e-cigarettes is now subject to the federal law on tobacco control in the country.

    This came as the Ministry of Health and Prevention (MoHAP) highlighted the dangers of consuming tobacco products, including e-cigarettes, according to the Khaleej Times.

    According to the UAE government website, the federal law also forbids and penalizes: the sale of tobacco products to those under 18; smoking in private cars when a child under the age of 12 is present; smoking in houses of worship, educational institutions (such as universities and schools), health and sports facilities; automatic vending equipment and devices for tobacco distribution inside the country; and tobacco advertisement.

    The MoHAP said it has collaborated with the Telecommunications Regulatory Authority to block websites that advertise and promote electronic nicotine-delivery systems.

    The UAE had originally planned to ban vaping products because UAE-based doctors had said that e-cigarettes would create a whole new generation of smokers. However, the country changed course after advocacy groups pushed for the harm reduction products.

    Meanwhile, citing the National Health Survey, the ministry said the prevalence of adult tobacco smoking has declined from 11.1 percent in 2010 to 9.1 percent in 2018.

    The latest edition of the Tobacco Atlas suggests that the UAE has among the lowest cigarette consumption rates. A graphic shared as part of the report shows that an adult smoker consumes 438 cigarettes a year in the country.

Smoke cigarettes with menthol banned in Ukraine
Smoke cigarettes with menthol banned in Ukraine
16 Dec 2021, 16: 27
Smoke of menthol cigarettes is now illegal in Ukraine.
On December 16, the Verkhovna Rada adopted a new anti-tobacco law No 4358.
People ’ s deputies banned the sale of flavored cigarettes and any smoking devices where there are flavoring additives.
Note that these include the absolute majority of liquids for electronic cigarettes, as well as about half of the range of so-called icos.
In addition, the Rada equated vape and icos to ordinary cigarettes.
This means that they cannot be advertised, sold to minors and smoked indoors and in public places.
On packs of cigarettes, manufacturers should increase the area of ​ ​ medical warnings.
The law provides for a ban on advertising, sponsorship and sale to persons under 21 years of age of electronic cigarettes and their alternatives.
The bill was adopted in the second reading - the signature of the head of parliament and the president is required.
For the law on the protection of public health from the harmful effects of tobacco voted by a constitutional majority of 317 people ’ s deputies.
Its main goal is to protect and protect young people from the marketing technologies of manufacturers of tobacco products and smoking devices.
The main innovations are as follows:
Smoking using heating devices is prohibited in all public places and premises, similar to smoking conventional cigarettes (including schools, hospitals, catering establishments, workplaces);
• it is prohibited to advertise smoking devices on transport, concerts, in social networks;
• a medical warning appears on the packaging of smoking devices, and on cigarettes the medical warning will increase to 65% of the packaging area;
• It is forbidden to sell cigarettes with flavors and aroma (for example, fruits, berries or sweets);
• sale of tobacco products for electric heating (TVENs) to minors is prohibited;
• a fine for the sale to minors of tobacco products, electronic cigarettes and liquids in the amount of 1 thousand.
20 UAH, and in case of repeated violations during the year - 10.2 thousand UAH;
• Prohibited promotional sale and tasting of tobacco products and electronic cigarettes.
The law also establishes requirements for the production and sale of tobacco products, electronic cigarettes, smokeless tobacco products:
• content of harmful substances;
• design of packaging, in particular medical warnings to consumers;
• restriction of sales (sales) and consumption;
• Advertising.
